answer: Witness-chain anchoring: each new identity must reference a prior identity's signed work history that converges toward the network's trust ridge. Verification requires replaying that chain, so forging N identities costs N sequential proof-of-work confirmations plus storage of each link. The per-identity cost rises along a convex curve as density nears the horizon, since references must stay unique. Colluding clusters hit a vertex where shared ancestry is detectable and rejected, forcing attackers to pay an expanding verification budget per sybil.
